nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily (titrate up to 10 mg as tolerated)
medications.purpose: Control hypertension, reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line treatment – ACE‑I for CKD with hypertension or ACR ≥30 mg/mmol

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent condition)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 650 mg (≈8 mmol) orally three times daily, titrate to maintain serum bicarbonate 22‑24 mmol/L
medications.duration: Until target bicarbonate achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Correct severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.00) associated with CKD stage 5
medications.nice_justification: CKD management guideline advises correction of metabolic acidosis to protect bone and muscle; consistent with NICE CKD recommendations

medications.dose: 50 IU/kg subcutaneously once weekly (after iron repletion)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10‑12 g/dL, then review every 2‑4 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA after iron repletion for CKD‑related anemia

medications.purpose: Manage hypertriglyceridaemia where fibrates are contraindicated
medications.nice_justification: Alternative lipid‑lowering therapy when fibrates contraindicated in eGFR <30 (NG203 contraindication list)

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; contraindicated with eGFR 6.5 mL/min/1.73 m²
Risk of lactic acidosis when eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or GLP‑1 receptor agonist (if not contraindicated)

contraindications.reason: eGFR <20 mL/min/1.73 m² – not indicated and ineffective
contraindications.alternative: Focus on ACE‑I and other CKD measures

contraindications.reason: Contra‑indicated in eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² per NG203
Dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury risk
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with prophylactic hydration if absolutely necessary

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure not recorded – obtain measurement before ACE‑I titration and set target <130/80 mmHg (or <140/90 mmHg if ACR <70 mg/mmol).
Serum potassium not available – order baseline K+ before starting Ramipril and repeat 1‑2 weeks after dose changes.
Liver function tests not available – obtain ALT/AST before initiating Atorvastatin.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – order before starting ESA; correct iron deficiency first.
Allergy history unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or ESA hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Volume status not documented – assess for fluid overload before starting sodium bicarbonate.
Patient’s exact ACR not provided – assume proteinuria present given active problem list; monitor ACR after ACE‑I initiation.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril and atorvastatin as first‑line CKD therapies per NG203, correct severe metabolic acidosis with oral sodium bicarbonate, address CKD‑related anemia with epoetin alfa after iron repletion, and manage hypertriglyceridaemia with omega‑3s. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, fibrates, dual ACE‑I/ARB, lithium and unprotected IV contrast. Monitor BP, serum K+, creatinine, liver enzymes, lipid profile, bicarbonate, and hemoglobin at recommended intervals and adjust therapy accordingly.
